messages.content: what are the tools u know for booking flights

function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common “tools” (websites, apps, APIs, and platforms) you can use to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use‑case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Online travel agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Aggregates flights, hotels, car rentals, packages. | One‑stop booking for multi‑service trips. |
| | **Kayak** | Flight comparison engine, price alerts, flexible date search. | Finding cheapest fares across many carriers. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global flight search, price alerts, multi‑city itineraries. | Great for budget travelers and flexible dates. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, “Explore” map, price tracking. | Quick fare comparison and itinerary planning. |
| | **Momondo** | Price comparison, “Price Calendar”, “Flight Finder”. | Useful for spotting hidden deals. |
| | **Priceline** | “Name Your Own Price”, “Express Deals”, package deals. | Good for last‑minute or bulk bookings. |
| | **Orbitz** | Loyalty program, bundle discounts. | Frequent traveler rewards. |
| | **Travelocity** | Similar to Orbitz, often bundled with Expedia. | One‑stop booking. |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” discounted fares, “Hot Deals” for hotels. | Cheap last‑minute flights. |
| | **CheapOair** | Discounted fares, promo codes. | Budget travelers. |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia, multi‑currency support. | International travelers, especially in Asia. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels but also offers flights. | One‑stop booking. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Price alerts, coupon codes. | Tracking specific routes. |
| | **Hipmunk** | “Best Time to Book” feature, “Smart Travel” algorithm. | Finding optimal travel times. |
| | **Travelzoo** | Curated deals, coupons. | Deal hunters. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Last‑minute deals, package bundles. | Impulse travelers. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA, multi‑currency. | European travelers. |
| | **eDreams** | Low‑cost fares, “eDreams Deals”. | Budget travelers. |
| | **TUI** | Package holidays, flights, hotels. | All‑in‑one holiday booking. |
| | **Travelgenio** | Multi‑currency, global coverage. | International travelers. |
| | **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network, flight data API. | Developers building flight‑search widgets. |
| | **Skiplagged** | Hidden‑city ticketing, price comparison. | Advanced fare hunting. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Price alerts, coupon codes. | Tracking specific routes. |
| | **FlightHub** | Low‑cost fares, “FlightHub Deals”. | Budget travelers. |
| | **JetRadar** | Real‑time flight search, price alerts. | Quick fare comparison. |
| | **FlightNetwork** | Low‑cost fares, “FlightNetwork Deals”. | Budget travelers. |
| | **FlightAware** | Flight status, real‑time tracking. | Monitoring flight progress. |
| | **FlightStats** | Flight status, historical data. | Business travelers. |

### 2. Airline‑direct booking tools

| Tool | What it offers | Why you’d use it |
|------|----------------|------------------|
| **Direct airline websites** (e.g., Delta, United, Lufthansa) | Full fare classes, loyalty points, seat selection, baggage options. | Best for frequent flyers who want to use miles or earn status. |
| **Airline mobile apps** | Push notifications for price drops, mobile‑only discounts, boarding passes. | Convenient for on‑the‑go travelers. |
| **Airline APIs** (e.g., Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) | Programmatic flight search, booking, and inventory management. | Used by travel agencies and developers building custom booking solutions. |
| **Airline loyalty portals** (e.g., MileagePlus, SkyMiles) | Redeem miles, upgrade offers, elite benefits. | For members looking to maximize rewards. |

---

### 3. Aggregator APIs & SDKs

| API / SDK | Key features | Typical use‑case |
|-----------|--------------|------------------|
| **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** | Flight search, booking, seat selection, dynamic pricing. | Building a travel app or integrating flight search into a website. |
| **Sabre APIs** | Comprehensive inventory, fare rules, booking, and ticketing. | Enterprise travel agencies, corporate booking systems. |
| **Travelport Universal API** | Unified access to multiple GDSs, booking, and ancillary services. | Multi‑carrier booking solutions. |
| **Skyscanner API** | Search, price alerts, multi‑city itineraries. | Price comparison widgets. |
| **Google Flights API** (via Google Cloud) | Flight search, price history, flight status. | Data analytics, price trend monitoring. |
| **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status, historical data, flight tracking. | Flight status dashboards, travel apps. |
| **OpenSky API** | Real‑time flight data, ADS-B. | Aviation enthusiasts, research. |

---

### 4. Mobile & Web Apps

| App | Strengths | Ideal users |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| **Hopper** | Predictive pricing, price alerts, best‑time‑to‑book. | Budget travelers, last‑minute planners. |
| **Airbnb Experiences** | Flights + experiences bundled. | Travelers wanting a complete trip package. |
| **Rome2rio** | Multi‑modal transport planner (flight, train, bus). | Complex itineraries, multi‑city trips. |
| **TripIt** | Trip organization, flight status alerts. | Busy professionals, frequent travelers. |
| **Google Trips** (now integrated into Google Travel) | Trip planning, itinerary suggestions. | Casual travelers. |
| **Kayak Explore** | Visual map of destinations by price. | Destination discovery. |

| Service | How it works | When to use |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| **Google Flights Alerts** | Email alerts for price changes on selected routes. | Long‑term planning, price monitoring. |
| **Skyscanner Price Alerts** | Push/email alerts for price drops. | Budget travelers. |
| **Hopper Alerts** | Predictive alerts for best booking time. | Long‑term planning. |
| **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for specific routes, coupon codes. | Deal hunters. |
| **FlightAware Alerts** | Flight status alerts, delays, cancellations. | Business travelers. |

---

## Quick Decision Guide

1. **You’re a frequent flyer** → Book directly on the airline’s site or use their mobile app to maximize miles and elite benefits.
2. **You’re looking for the cheapest fare** → Use a price‑comparison engine (Kayak, Skyscanner, Google Flights) and set price alerts.
3. **You’re building a travel app** → Integrate an API (Amadeus, Sabre, Skyscanner) for flight search and booking.
4. **You’re traveling with a group or company** → Use a corporate or group booking platform (Concur, Egencia, Group Travel Solutions).
5. **You want real‑time flight status** → Use FlightAware, FlightRadar24, or the airline’s status page.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific tool or how to integrate them into your workflow!
